haiku-low.q1: The 02:00 UTC scheduler starts it. It extracts orders from the read replica whose updated_at is after watermark minus 2h and up to the replica clock at snapshot open.
haiku-low.q2: Bulk imports hold transactions open up to 90 min, and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit. Rows can reach the replica up to 90 minutes late.
haiku-low.q3: The app bumps updated_at on every write, so the row returns in the next night's extract. The merge overwrites the old copy because its updated_at is newer.
haiku-low.q4: The app sets deleted_at, which flows through the same extract and merge. The warehouse row becomes is_deleted = true. Nothing is ever hard-deleted from fact_orders.
haiku-low.q5: The attempt's transaction never commits, so target and watermark are untouched. It retries up to 3 tries total, 15 minutes apart. After the 3rd failure, on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the last committed data. The 06:00 check posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts when etl_runs has no successful try for tonight.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday recon job reloads it, if the order was created in the last 30 days and Sunday's nightly succeeded. Recon compares counts and checksums and reloads mismatched days.
haiku-low.q8: The merge keys on order_id. It inserts new ids, and overwrites existing rows only when the staged updated_at is strictly newer than the target's. Otherwise the row is skipped.
haiku-low.q9: It is stored in etl_watermark, a single warehouse row. The upper bound (replica clock at snapshot open) is written in the same transaction as the merge and success status, on commit.
haiku-low.q10: The merge, the watermark write and the run's success status commit in one transaction. Dashboards read only fact_orders, so they see the whole night or none of it.
haiku-low.q11: Staging is cleared at the start of every try, so the failed attempt's staged data is discarded. The retry reads the same checkpoint and extracts from watermark minus 2h to a fresh upper bound.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads all orders created that day from the replica, lands them in cleared stg, and applies them through the same merge in its own transaction. It does not move the nightly high-water mark.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler kicks it off at 02:00 UTC. It reads the read replica only and extracts orders whose updated_at is after (watermark minus 2h) and up to the replica's clock when the snapshot opens.
sonnet.q2: Bulk imports in the app hold transactions open for up to 90 min, and updated_at is stamped when the row is written, not at commit. So the rows can show up on the replica up to 90 min late.
sonnet.q3: The app bumps updated_at on every write, so the edited row comes back in the next night's extract. The merge overwrites the old version because the staged updated_at is strictly newer.
sonnet.q4: The app sets deleted_at (a soft delete, a write that bumps updated_at) and never hard-deletes. It comes through the normal load and becomes is_deleted = true on the warehouse row. Nothing is ever deleted from fact_orders.
sonnet.q5: The transaction never commits, so the target and HWM are untouched. It retries after 15 min, up to 3 tries per night. After the 3rd failure on-call is paged.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards refresh at 06:00 UTC regardless and show the last committed data. The 06:00 check finds no successful try for tonight in etl_runs and posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts. If the retries were exhausted, on-call was already paged.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday recon job. It covers orders created in the last 30 days and only runs if Sunday's nightly succeeded. It finds the day's row count/checksum mismatch and reloads that day's orders.
sonnet.q8: The merge is keyed on order_id. Existing ids are overwritten only when the staged updated_at is strictly newer than the target's. Otherwise the row is skipped.
sonnet.q9: It is in the warehouse, in etl_watermark (a single row). The value written is the upper bound, the replica's clock when the snapshot opened. It is written inside the same transaction as the merge and the run's success status.
sonnet.q10: The merge, the HWM write and the success status are one transaction, so the target changes all at once or not at all. Dashboards read only fact_orders, never the landing table, so they see the whole night or none of it.
sonnet.q11: The retry clears stg first, so the staged data is discarded. It reads the same checkpoint (watermark minus 2h as lower bound) and takes a fresh upper bound (the replica's clock when the new snapshot opens).
sonnet.q12: For each mismatched day it re-reads every order created that day from the replica, into stg_orders (cleared first). It pushes them through the same merge as the nightly, in its own transaction, so an older copy can't win. It never moves the checkpoint.
